title: world_genesis/1 — ONE world's FICTION, authored from a user's brief: who is here, what the places are, what happened before, and who came away knowing it. Never structure. No uuid, no coordinate, no tick, no radius, no count, no number of any kind appears anywhere in this schema, because the engine owns all of it: ids come from gen_random_uuid(), footprints from fn_extent_class_metres + fn_area_around, time from the genesis tick ladder, acceptance from the gate. Qualities the engine needs numerically (a trait's strength, how malleable a mind is) are emitted as CLASSES from closed enums and mapped by the engine, exactly as extent_class already works for place_author. Cross-references between parts use canonical_name, the only join key the seat can express; every reference must resolve or the build is refused. Array ceilings bound COST, not shape — they are not a statement about what a world usually contains (GA-2/GA-3).

display_name.description: What this world is called. The directory shows it.

tagline.description: One line of fiction about the world, in the world's own voice. Authored, never composed from the brief verbatim.

mood.description: One word for the world's atmosphere, free vocabulary (the theme is deliberately not enum-validated: unknown values degrade, never fail).

ornament.description: One word for the world's visual register. Free vocabulary, same reason as mood.

region.description: The parent place every other place sits inside — a quarter, a valley, a station, a district. The engine draws its footprint from extent_class and places the children within it.

places.description: The rooms of the opening world. At least two, because a world with one room has no way out and cannot be travelled (the SPEC-030 floor).

descriptor.description: How a stranger seeing this place for the first time would name it. This is what renders before anyone has earned its name.

canonical_name.description: The place's true name, and the join key other parts reference. Never shown to a viewer who has not earned it.

kind.description: A short genre-agnostic label for what sort of place this is. Never a genre-locked noun.

description.description: What is concretely here — surfaces, exits, objects, light, smell. The narrator reads this; when it is thin the narrator invents, so make it load-bearing.

ways.description: How the places join. Each becomes a portal artifact; without at least one, no one can leave the room they start in.

descriptor.description: A door, a hatch, a stair, a gap in the fence — what a stranger sees.

to_place.description: canonical_name of a different place in `places`.

cast.description: Everyone in the world except the player. At least one: a world with nobody in it is legal but inert.

descriptor.description: How a stranger sees this person before learning anything — 'a hooded figure by the bar'. This is what renders until the player earns the name, so it must stand alone as an introduction.

canonical_name.description: Their true name, and the join key other parts reference.

standing.description: What they do and where they sit in this world's order, in a phrase.

speech_manner.description: How they talk — clipped, formal, wheedling, flat. The cognition seats read this.

manner.description: How that disposition shows in behaviour.

hiding.description: The one thing this person knows and does not say. It becomes a private perception only they hold — the planted secret the engine's own I-3 test hunts for leaks of.

starts_in.description: canonical_name of the place they are in when the player walks in.

objects.description: Things that matter — a ledger, a key, a sealed note, a crate. Not scenery: scenery belongs in a place's description.

where.description: Exactly one of `in_place` or `carried_by`. An object must be somewhere findable.

history.description: What happened before the player arrived, oldest first. The engine assigns each one a tick in ascending order below the arrival; the seat states only the ORDER by position in this array. Every piece of knowledge anyone holds at genesis must come from one of these — knowledge is authored WITH its path, never as a free-floating fact (B-2, B-7).

what_happened.description: The event, stated as world truth in one sentence.

where.description: canonical_name of the place it happened in.

knowledge.description: Who came away knowing, in what way, and what they took from it. NOTHING may name the player: the player was not there and holds no perception of any of this.

content.description: What they believe, in their own terms — not a summary of the event, but what they took from it.

arrival.description: The player walking in. This is a PREMISE, not a mind: the player gets a name and a way of being seen, and nothing else. No traits, no disposition, no personality — the engine refuses to write an inner state for the player (B-4).

descriptor.description: How the room sees the stranger who just walked in.

canonical_name.description: The player's name. Nobody in the world holds a perception of it — no one here knows who walked in.

place.description: canonical_name of the place they walk into. AT LEAST ONE member of `cast` MUST have `starts_in` equal to this exact place — the visitor walks in on people, never into an empty room they must then search. This is validated and a mismatch is rejected.

stated.description: The arrival in the player's own first person — 'I stepped into the Drowned Lantern.' This becomes their single perception, and it is the only thing they know.

why.description: Why they are here, as premise. Never an interior state, never a feeling — a situation.

extent_class.description: A size CLASS, qualitative. The engine turns it into metres.

tension.description: How pressed this place feels. The engine turns it into the beat budget; an unstamped room would get an infinite one.

way_state.description: open: passable. shut: closed but openable. locked: needs something. The engine writes {open, locked} from this.

strength.description: A qualitative magnitude. The engine maps it to the number the schema forbids the seat from emitting.

epistemic_type.description: How this holder came to know, from the canonical enum (01_epistemic_type_canonical_enum.md). 'direct' means they were there. The play-time transitions (shared/mistaken/confirmed/disputed) are not authorable at genesis: nothing has been contested yet.
